items.problem: SKILL.md's navigation invariant #4 ('Deferred items are omitted from the navigation surface') directly contradicts the skill's own placeholder guidance (SKILL.md L229-236, MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md L57-65), which says a page whose hero control is unsupported must be KEPT with a visible placeholder. Facing the contradiction, the agent applied invariant #4 to the whole InkCanvas scenario page and dropped it.
items.evidence: SKILL.md L109 'Deferred items are omitted from the navigation surface'; SKILL.md L229-236 'This applies equally to a page whose hero control was deferred ... Leave a visible declarative placeholder'; session-log.txt only 4 scenarios registered.
items.covered_at: SKILL.md Step 1 'Navigation invariants' (L104-109), bullet #4; cross-referenced placeholder guidance at SKILL.md L229-236 and MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md #cs0246 (L57-65).
items.why_missed: grey-zone / ambiguous — 'defer the file' and 'keep the page with a placeholder' both plausibly apply to a scenario page whose hero control is unsupported, with no rule stating which wins.
items.proposed_improvement: Sharpen invariant #4 (and the `defer` triage bullet at L88) to state the tie-break explicitly: only omit a scenario from navigation when it has NO representable UI at all; a scenario whose only blocker is an unsupported hero control STAYS in navigation with a placeholder, so the migrated app keeps the same scenario count as the source.
items.generalizes: Every sample-style UWP app maps scenarios 1:1 to nav entries; a clear 'keep the scenario, placeholder the control' rule prevents scenario-count regressions across all of them, not just InkCanvas.
